title: CI tests, coverage, and historical quality metrics
description:
What this story is in Compass BE

Add a backend-quality reporting layer that fits the current NestJS codebase and deployment flow.

Today this repository already has:
- Jest-based unit tests via `npm test`
- Jest coverage via `npm run test:cov`
- separate e2e tests via `npm run test:e2e`
- repository testing and controller/service spec patterns documented in `docs/TESTING.md`
- code structure and architecture conventions documented in `docs/CODE_STANDARD.md`
- a GitHub Actions deploy workflow at `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`
- AWS OIDC already used in GitHub Actions for deploy
- an Admin API under `src/admin`
- DynamoDB table constants centralized in `src/database/tables.ts`
- existing periodic/backfill-style patterns such as `OnModuleInit` services and cron-enabled services when `CRON_ENABLED` is on

What is missing is a product-facing and reviewer-facing quality view:
- PRs do not currently show a dedicated quality summary for test + coverage outcomes
- deploy workflow does not currently have a distinct quality gate step before deploy
- there is no persisted historical store of backend quality snapshots
- Admin does not yet expose historical quality records

Desired outcome

1. CI quality checks for meaningful code changes
Add a dedicated GitHub Actions quality workflow/job that runs the existing backend checks in a way that matches this codebase:
- install dependencies
- run lint
- run unit tests with coverage (`npm run test:cov`)
- run e2e tests (`npm run test:e2e`)

This should be designed so it can run on pull requests and on the branches that matter for deploys (`dev`, `staging`, `main`, and optionally `feature/**` if we want parity with the deploy workflow).

2. PR-visible quality reporting
Publish test and coverage results directly into GitHub pull requests. Codecov is the default choice for coverage reporting because it gives PR annotations, status checks, and historical coverage comparison without us having to build that UI ourselves.

For this repository, the output should at minimum make these visible on the PR:
- whether lint passed
- whether unit tests passed
- whether e2e tests passed
- coverage summary / delta for the backend coverage report generated by Jest

3. Configurable PR enforcement
The quality job/check must support two operating modes:
- informational only: workflow posts status/comment/checks but is not a required merge gate
- enforced: branch protection / required status checks block merge when quality fails

Important implementation note for this codebase: the backend should not try to enforce merge policy itself. The repository should expose stable GitHub check names, and enforcement should be configured through GitHub branch protection / required checks plus documented repository variables/secrets if needed.

4. Persist historical backend quality snapshots in DynamoDB
Create a dedicated DynamoDB table for historical backend quality snapshots:
- table name constant: `AppQuality`
- records stored per backend version/build snapshot

Because this backend already stores application/config/statistics-style data in DynamoDB, this feature should follow the project’s existing repository/service/module pattern rather than adding ad-hoc scripts.

Each quality record should capture enough information for Admin trend views, for example:
- backend version identifier
- branch / branch class if available
- environment if available (`dev`, `staging`, `prod`)
- commit SHA if available
- recordedAt timestamp
- lint status
- unit test status and summary counts
- e2e test status and summary counts
- coverage summary fields (at least statements / branches / functions / lines percentages)
- source of record (CI, startup backfill, manual if we later need it)

5. Admin API access to quality history
Expose quality history through the existing Admin module (`src/admin`) so Admin clients can query historical quality records.

The first version should support listing records, ideally newest-first, with the same general pagination style already used elsewhere in Admin (`limit`, `nextCursor`). Filtering by environment and/or branch class is a useful stretch goal, but the core requirement is a reliable list endpoint for historical comparisons.

6. Startup backfill behavior for current backend version
On backend startup, check whether a quality record already exists for the current backend version/build identifier. If not, create one.

For this codebase, this should reuse existing Nest patterns such as `OnModuleInit` / bootstrap-time service orchestration, and it must be careful not to block startup with expensive test execution.

Important codebase-specific constraint:
- the running Nest app should not execute the full Jest suite on startup
- startup backfill should only persist an already-produced quality snapshot for the current version, or a minimal placeholder/summary derived from build-produced artifacts/config that were generated earlier in CI/deploy

This means the implementation likely needs a small handoff artifact from CI/build into runtime, or a runtime-readable summary payload, rather than trying to run tests inside the app process.

Testing and implementation standards for this story

All code added for this story must follow the repository conventions documented in `docs/CODE_STANDARD.md` and include automated tests consistent with `docs/TESTING.md`.

That means, for this story:
- controllers, services, repositories, DTOs, parsers, and startup orchestration should follow existing NestJS module/repository/token patterns
- new routes and DTOs should include explicit Swagger decorators
- unit tests should be atomic and colocated as `*.spec.ts`
- external dependencies must be mocked in unit tests; no live AWS SDK or external services in unit tests
- new logic should include happy-path, edge-case, and error-path coverage where meaningful
- if this story introduces public/admin API changes, e2e coverage should be added or updated where appropriate

Acceptance criteria refined for Compass BE

- A GitHub Actions quality workflow/job exists and runs lint, unit tests with coverage, and e2e tests for relevant PRs/branches.
- Pull requests show backend quality results, including coverage reporting.
- The repository exposes stable quality checks so merge enforcement can be turned on/off using GitHub branch protection rather than code changes.
- A new DynamoDB table `AppQuality` exists in the backend table constants and corresponding persistence layer.
- Backend quality snapshots are persisted in `AppQuality` with version/build metadata plus test and coverage summary fields.
- The Admin API exposes an endpoint to list historical quality records.
- On backend startup, the app checks for a record for the current backend version/build and writes one if missing, without running Jest inside the application process.
- New backend code added for this story is covered by automated tests consistent with `docs/TESTING.md`, including repository/service/controller/startup behavior as applicable.
- New code for this story follows repository standards documented in `docs/CODE_STANDARD.md`.
- Documentation explains how Codecov/GitHub quality reporting, testing expectations, and merge enforcement are configured for this repository.

Implementation notes / likely code touchpoints

- standards/testing docs: `docs/CODE_STANDARD.md`, `docs/TESTING.md`
- CI/workflows: `.github/workflows/`
- test commands/config: `package.json`, `jest.config.js`, `tests/e2e/jest.e2e.json`
- persistence/table constants: `src/database/tables.ts`
- new module/repository/service: likely a new `src/app-quality` area following current module conventions
- admin exposure: `src/admin/admin.controller.ts`, `src/admin/admin.service.ts`, `src/admin/admin.module.ts`
- startup/backfill hook: a service using `OnModuleInit` or equivalent app bootstrap lifecycle
- environment/config additions if needed: `src/environment/environment.configuration.ts`, `src/environment/validation.ts`

Non-goals / guardrails

- Do not replace existing deploy OIDC flow; extend around it.
- Do not make the Nest runtime responsible for actually executing the project’s test suite.
- Do not hard-code GitHub branch protection behavior in backend code; document and support it via check names and repository settings.
- Do not build a large custom coverage UI in backend/Admin if Codecov already covers PR visualization well; backend persistence is for product-side historical querying.

features.title: Add a dedicated GitHub quality workflow for lint, unit coverage, and e2e tests
features.description:
Create a GitHub Actions workflow under `.github/workflows/` that runs the backend quality checks already supported by this repository: `npm run lint`, `npm run test:cov`, and `npm run test:e2e`. It should trigger for pull requests and relevant long-lived branches (`dev`, `staging`, `main`; optionally `feature/**` if we want parity with deploy behavior). The workflow should produce stable check names suitable for branch protection and should fail fast when quality checks fail before deploy-related steps are considered.

Implementation for this feature must follow `docs/CODE_STANDARD.md` for repository conventions and any helper logic/scripts added for workflow orchestration must include automated tests consistent with `docs/TESTING.md`. If this feature introduces workflow helper scripts, summary generators, or result-normalization code, those units should be covered with atomic `*.spec.ts` tests for success and failure paths.

features.title: Publish PR-visible coverage and quality results with Codecov and stable GitHub checks
features.description:
Extend the quality workflow so pull requests expose reviewer-facing quality output instead of only pass/fail logs. Upload the Jest coverage report produced by `npm run test:cov` to Codecov, and ensure the workflow surfaces distinct results for lint, unit tests, and e2e tests. The implementation should keep merge enforcement outside backend code: branch protection can later require these stable checks, while the workflow itself remains usable in informational-only mode.

Implementation for this feature must follow `docs/CODE_STANDARD.md`, and any new parsing, summarization, or artifact-generation logic added to support PR-visible reporting must have automated tests consistent with `docs/TESTING.md`. If coverage summaries or quality results are transformed in backend-owned scripts/code, add atomic `*.spec.ts` coverage for happy-path, malformed-input, and failure scenarios.

features.title: Implement AppQuality persistence and a CI/runtime snapshot contract
features.description:
Add a new backend-quality persistence area following existing DynamoDB repository patterns. Introduce the `AppQuality` table constant in `src/database/tables.ts`, define the quality snapshot model/repository/service/module, and persist records containing version/build metadata, commit information when available, environment, branch metadata, lint/unit/e2e outcomes, coverage percentages, recordedAt, and source. The implementation should define a runtime-readable artifact or payload format produced by CI/build so the application can store an already-produced quality snapshot without executing tests at runtime.

Implementation for this feature must follow `docs/CODE_STANDARD.md`, including module/service/repository/token structure, explicit DTO modeling, and keeping AWS access inside repository/provider layers. Add automated tests consistent with `docs/TESTING.md`, including atomic `*.spec.ts` coverage for repository behavior, service behavior, artifact-to-model mapping/validation, and relevant error or malformed-data scenarios. External dependencies must be mocked; no live AWS SDK calls are allowed in unit tests.

features.title: Expose AppQuality history through Admin and backfill the current version on startup
features.description:
Integrate the new quality persistence layer into the running NestJS app. Add an Admin-facing endpoint under `src/admin` to list historical AppQuality records newest-first with the same pagination style already used elsewhere (`limit`, `nextCursor`). Then add a startup hook, using existing Nest lifecycle patterns, that checks whether a record exists for the current backend build/version and writes one if missing using the pre-produced quality snapshot artifact or a minimal runtime-readable summary. The startup path must not execute Jest or other expensive CI checks inside the application process. Update README/docs to explain the quality workflow, Codecov setup, the artifact handoff into runtime, and how merge enforcement is configured through GitHub branch protection rather than backend code.

Implementation for this feature must follow `docs/CODE_STANDARD.md`, including explicit Swagger decorators for new Admin DTOs/routes and existing controller/service/module conventions. Add automated tests consistent with `docs/TESTING.md`, including controller and service unit tests, startup lifecycle tests for record-exists / record-missing / artifact-missing behavior, and e2e coverage updates where appropriate for the new Admin endpoint. External dependencies must be mocked in unit tests.
